messages.text: Zegallan banners from the last war hang above the palace map table. King Alexander names the villages lost on the Ashen March while Prince Forre marks a road to Fort Vicinitas in ink. Vallie has brought the Guild charter: the Crown wants a free company that can go where its army cannot. The council falls quiet, and every face at the table turns to you.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Princess Haley, do you believe the rumour about your mother?

messages.name: Haley
messages.text:
Haley's knuckles whiten against her fan. A beat, and her voice is ice. "The rumours are—" Her eyes flash. "The rumours are childish and base." Her posture stiffens as she turns her gaze from the King, from Forre, from Vallie. "My mother is not—" She stops, the words catching. The King's face is stone. Prince Forre's eyes are unreadable.
And Haley's jaw sets. She breathes, slow and quiet. She does not speak further.

messages.name: Alexander
messages.text:
Alexander's dark eyes narrow, and his hand falls away from the map table. "The Princess believes—" He doesn't finish the word. His face hardens, and a voice that has commanded armies rises. "This is a war council, not a gossip's den."
The King stands, and the silver of his crown gleams in the shadow of the Zegallan banners. "The missing dead will be looked into. But the matter is not here."
His gaze is not on Haley. It is on you. "The commission is this: Greywater, the Ashen March, the missing dead. The Guild's charter will see you through."
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do you accept?"

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Guildmaster Vallie, what is the Crown really asking of adventurers?

messages.name: Vallie
messages.text:
Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Crown's asking for a scalpel," she says, her voice blunt and low. "Where Forre's army goes in with a hammer, you're the ones who sneak in. The missing dead? That's what they want you to investigate. But make no mistake—they're sending you into the Empire's teeth."
She glances at the King, her expression unreadable. "The Crown will pay you, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park. It's a foray into enemy territory. You'll be behind their lines, and if you get caught..." She trails off, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room. "You'll be on your own."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: So who is burning the villages behind the line?

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
A murmur passes through the councillors. Haley's hand tightens on her fan, and Forre's green eyes flicker to the King.
"A winged herald calling himself a servant of Prodyr," Alexander says, his voice cold. "He claims to be a divine messenger. The villages he burns are—" He doesn't finish. "He is the Empire's weapon."
Vallie's eye narrows. "One he can't control." She glances at the party. "And that's why they want you. Soldiers fight armies. You hunt monsters."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Prince Forre, what did your runner just tell you? And Your Majesty, how far east has the line slipped?

messages.name: Forre
messages.text:
Forre's head tilts, and he doesn't look up from the map. "A messenger's duty is to deliver news, not to explain it." His emerald eyes are fixed on the black token.
He traces the line of the token's new position with a fingertip, and doesn't smile. "The runner says the western front has moved. That's all."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."

messages.name: Alexander
messages.text:
Alexander does not move. His hand rests on the table, and his face is stone.
"The line has not slipped," he says, and his voice is low. "The line is where I say it is."
He looks at Forre, and his eyes are dark. "You will not tell me we are losing the war."
The King stands, his white fur mantle shifting, and the air in the room is cold. "The line will hold at Fort Vicinitas."
He looks at the party. "And this is why you will go to Greywater. To find the missing dead."
A beat, and his face hardens. "And to end this rumour."

messages.text: Guildmaster, be straight with me. Does the Guild think this commission is worth our lives?

messages.name: Vallie

"The Guild's thinking is this: The Crown will pay you for this job, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park." Her voice is blunt and low. "You're being sent behind their lines, and if you get caught..."

messages.text: Belle, you've been quiet. What do you think of this King and his war?

messages.name: Belle
messages.text:

A beat, and her grin is all teeth. "And I'll have my axe in the skulls of that winged herald if he shows his face."

messages.text: Prince Forre, you let that rumour about the Queen run through camp. Why haven't you put it down?

messages.name: Forre
messages.text:

He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The court speaks. The court whispers. The court lies."
He doesn't say anything else.

messages.text: Has anyone actually seen where the dead go after they leave their graves?

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The question hangs in the air, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room.

The King stands still, his face a mask, his gaze fixed on the map table where the Zegallan banner hangs above.
A beat, and he speaks, his voice low and flat. "No one."
He looks at you, his eyes dark. "No one has seen where they go."
And the silence stretches, and the King does not look away.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.

messages.text: Belle, Dalan, get the horses. We ride for Fort Vicinitas tonight.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride through the gate and report to whoever commands Fort Vicinitas.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The horses' hooves clatter on the stone as the party passes through the gate. The sentry steps aside, his spear-tip lowered.
The courtyard is empty, save for a few soldiers who are just stirring.
A man in plate armour stands at the far end of the courtyard, his face grim and his eyes hard. He is watching the party approach.
His armour is scarred and dented, and a longsword hangs at his hip.
He does not move as the party approaches, but his gaze is fixed on them.
And his voice is low and flat.
"You're the Crown's free company."
He doesn't wait for an answer.
"I am Captain Kaelen. I command this fort."
He looks at the party, his gaze lingering on Belle and Dalan.
"The Prince will be here by noon. Until then, you are under my command."
He looks at you.
"And we have much to discuss."

messages.text: Princess Haley, do you believe the rumour about your mother?

"The Crown's asking for a scalpel," she says, her voice blunt and low. "Where Forre's army goes in with a hammer, you're the ones who sneak in. The missing dead? That's what they want you to investigate. But make no mistake—they're sending you into the Empire's teeth."

He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."

messages.text: We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.

messages.text:
The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.

messages.text: Prince Forre, what did your runner just tell you? And Your Majesty, how far east has the line slipped?

messages.name: Forre
messages.text:

He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.

She turns, and her boots are heavy as she heads for the ridge.
"And as for the flag—" She stops, and looks at Dalan. "Find a white flag. We're not asking for anything."
She looks at you, and her expression is sharp. "We're just going to be there. And we'll see what they say."

messages.text:
Kanna drives Blood Oath into the mud, her dark red eyes narrowing. "LOUD and fuckin' plain, then. You bury yours, I bury mine. My regiment keeps Greywater. Break it and I break you. I keep my word."
The Zegallan banner flutters in the wind, and there is no mistaking the sign.
A beat, and she shifts her weight. "And you've been diggin' up our dead at Greywater, too. Some new kind of sick-fuck game?"
The black steel of her armour gleams in the dawn light. "Or maybe the Darrans finally got the balls to send in someone worth killin'."
A beat, and her voice drops. "Which one is it?"

messages.text: Zegallan banners from the last war hang above the palace map table. King Alexander names the villages lost on the Ashen March while Prince Forre marks a road to Fort Vicinitas in ink. messages.text: Princess Haley, do you believe the rumour about your mother?

And Haley's jaw sets. She breathes, slow and quiet. She does not speak further.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Guildmaster Vallie, what is the Crown really asking of adventurers?

messages.name: Vallie
messages.text:
Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Crown's asking for a scalpel," she says, her voice blunt and low. "Where Forre's army goes in with a hammer, you're the ones who sneak in. The missing dead? That's what they want you to investigate. But make no mistake—they're sending you into the Empire's teeth."
She glances at the King, her expression unreadable. "The Crown will pay you, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park. It's a foray into enemy territory. You'll be behind their lines, and if you get caught..." She trails off, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room. "You'll be on your own."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Prince Forre, what did your runner just tell you? And Your Majesty, how far east has the line slipped?

messages.name: Forre
messages.text:
Forre's head tilts, and he doesn't look up from the map. "A messenger's duty is to deliver news, not to explain it." His emerald eyes are fixed on the black token.
He traces the line of the token's new position with a fingertip, and doesn't smile. "The runner says the western front has moved. That's all."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."

messages.text: We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.

A beat, and her voice drops. "Which one is it?"

messages.text:
Belle doesn't turn around. Her hand is still on Cleaver's haft, and her jaw is set, and she's not smiling.
"Not us." She says it flat and hard. "We're here on a job from the Crown, and we're looking for the missing dead, not diggin' 'em up."

And her voice drops. "Because if we're both losing our dead, then neither of us is winning."

messages.text: Princess Haley, do you believe the rumour about your mother?

messages.name: Haley
messages.text:
Haley's knuckles whiten against her fan. A beat, and her voice is ice. "The rumours are—" Her eyes flash. "The rumours are childish and base." Her posture stiffens as she turns her gaze from the King, from Forre, from Vallie. "My mother is not—" She stops, the words catching. The King's face is stone. Prince Forre's eyes are unreadable.
And Haley's jaw sets. She breathes, slow and quiet. She does not speak further.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Guildmaster Vallie, what is the Crown really asking of adventurers?

messages.name: Vallie
messages.text:
Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Crown's asking for a scalpel," she says, her voice blunt and low. "Where Forre's army goes in with a hammer, you're the ones who sneak in. The missing dead? That's what they want you to investigate. But make no mistake—they're sending you into the Empire's teeth."
She glances at the King, her expression unreadable. "The Crown will pay you, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park. It's a foray into enemy territory. You'll be behind their lines, and if you get caught..." She trails off, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room. "You'll be on your own."

messages.text:

"A winged herald calling himself a servant of Prodyr," Alexander says, his voice cold. "He claims to be a divine messenger. The villages he burns are—" He doesn't finish. "He is the Empire's weapon."

messages.name: Forre
messages.text:
Forre's head tilts, and he doesn't look up from the map. "A messenger's duty is to deliver news, not to explain it." His emerald eyes are fixed on the black token.
He traces the line of the token's new position with a fingertip, and doesn't smile. "The runner says the western front has moved. That's all."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."

messages.text: Belle, you've been quiet. What do you think of this King and his war?

messages.name: Belle
messages.text:

She looks at Max, then at the map. "We'll go behind the lines, find what's missing, and bring it back."
A beat, and her grin is all teeth. "And I'll have my axe in the skulls of that winged herald if he shows his face."

messages.text: Prince Forre, you let that rumour about the Queen run through camp. Why haven't you put it down?

messages.name: Forre
messages.text:
Forre's green eyes flicker up from the map, and he doesn't smile. "A rumour is a fire. You don't put it out by pouring water on it. You starve it of oxygen."
He looks back at the map, his finger tracing the line of the token. "And I am not in the business of extinguishing fires that warm my house."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The court speaks. The court whispers. The court lies."
He doesn't say anything else.

messages.text: Has anyone actually seen where the dead go after they leave their graves?

messages.text:

A beat, and he speaks, his voice low and flat. "No one."
He looks at you, his eyes dark. "No one has seen where they go."
And the silence stretches, and the King does not look away.

messages.text: Belle, Dalan, get the horses. We ride for Fort Vicinitas tonight.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride through the gate and report to whoever commands Fort Vicinitas.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The horses' hooves clatter on the stone as the party passes through the gate. The sentry steps aside, his spear-tip lowered.
The courtyard is empty, save for a few soldiers who are just stirring.
A man in plate armour stands at the far end of the courtyard, his face grim and his eyes hard. He is watching the party approach.
His armour is scarred and dented, and a longsword hangs at his hip.
He does not move as the party approaches, but his gaze is fixed on them.
And his voice is low and flat.
"You're the Crown's free company."
He doesn't wait for an answer.
"I am Captain Kaelen. I command this fort."
He looks at the party, his gaze lingering on Belle and Dalan.
"The Prince will be here by noon. Until then, you are under my command."
He looks at you.
"And we have much to discuss."

messages.text: Princess Haley, do you believe the rumour about your mother?

messages.text:
Haley's knuckles whiten against her fan. A beat, and her voice is ice. "The rumours are—" Her eyes flash. "The rumours are childish and base." Her posture stiffens as she turns her gaze from the King, from Forre, from Vallie. "My mother is not—" She stops, the words catching. The King's face is stone. Prince Forre's eyes are unreadable.
And Haley's jaw sets. She breathes, slow and quiet. She does not speak further.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Guildmaster Vallie, what is the Crown really asking of adventurers?

messages.name: Vallie
messages.text:
Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Crown's asking for a scalpel," she says, her voice blunt and low. "Where Forre's army goes in with a hammer, you're the ones who sneak in. The missing dead? That's what they want you to investigate. But make no mistake—they're sending you into the Empire's teeth."

messages.text:

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Prince Forre, what did your runner just tell you? And Your Majesty, how far east has the line slipped?

messages.name: Forre
messages.text:
Forre's head tilts, and he doesn't look up from the map. "A messenger's duty is to deliver news, not to explain it." His emerald eyes are fixed on the black token.
He traces the line of the token's new position with a fingertip, and doesn't smile. "The runner says the western front has moved. That's all."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.

She turns, and her boots are heavy as she heads for the ridge.
"And as for the flag—" She stops, and looks at Dalan. "Find a white flag. We're not asking for anything."
She looks at you, and her expression is sharp. "We're just going to be there. And we'll see what they say."

messages.name: Kanna
messages.text:
Kanna drives Blood Oath into the mud, her dark red eyes narrowing. "LOUD and fuckin' plain, then. You bury yours, I bury mine. My regiment keeps Greywater. Break it and I break you. I keep my word."
The Zegallan banner flutters in the wind, and there is no mistaking the sign.
A beat, and she shifts her weight. "And you've been diggin' up our dead at Greywater, too. Some new kind of sick-fuck game?"
The black steel of her armour gleams in the dawn light. "Or maybe the Darrans finally got the balls to send in someone worth killin'."
A beat, and her voice drops. "Which one is it?"

messages.name: Belle
messages.text:
Belle doesn't turn around. Her hand is still on Cleaver's haft, and her jaw is set, and she's not smiling.
"Not us." She says it flat and hard. "We're here on a job from the Crown, and we're looking for the missing dead, not diggin' 'em up."
A beat, and she shifts her weight. "So maybe you should stop caring about what the Darrans are doing, and start caring about where your own dead are going."
And her eyes are sharp. "Because if your dead are leaving the pits, and our dead are leaving our graves, then maybe we've got the same problem."
A beat, and she looks at Kanna. "And maybe we should be talking about that, not about who's digging where."
And her voice drops. "Because if we're both losing our dead, then neither of us is winning."

messages.text: Zegallan banners from the last war hang above the palace map table. King Alexander names the villages lost on the Ashen March while Prince Forre marks a road to Fort Vicinitas in ink. messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Princess Haley, do you believe the rumour about your mother?

messages.name: Haley
messages.text:
Haley's knuckles whiten against her fan. A beat, and her voice is ice. "The rumours are—" Her eyes flash. "The rumours are childish and base." Her posture stiffens as she turns her gaze from the King, from Forre, from Vallie. "My mother is not—" She stops, the words catching. The King's face is stone. Prince Forre's eyes are unreadable.
And Haley's jaw sets. She breathes, slow and quiet. She does not speak further.

messages.name: Alexander
messages.text:
Alexander's dark eyes narrow, and his hand falls away from the map table. "The Princess believes—" He doesn't finish the word. His face hardens, and a voice that has commanded armies rises. "This is a war council, not a gossip's den."
The King stands, and the silver of his crown gleams in the shadow of the Zegallan banners. "The missing dead will be looked into. But the matter is not here."
His gaze is not on Haley. It is on you. "The commission is this: Greywater, the Ashen March, the missing dead. The Guild's charter will see you through."
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do you accept?"

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Guildmaster Vallie, what is the Crown really asking of adventurers?

messages.name: Vallie
messages.text:
Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Crown's asking for a scalpel," she says, her voice blunt and low. "Where Forre's army goes in with a hammer, you're the ones who sneak in. The missing dead? That's what they want you to investigate. But make no mistake—they're sending you into the Empire's teeth."
She glances at the King, her expression unreadable. "The Crown will pay you, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park. It's a foray into enemy territory. You'll be behind their lines, and if you get caught..." She trails off, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room. "You'll be on your own."

messages.text: So who is burning the villages behind the line?

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
A murmur passes through the councillors. Haley's hand tightens on her fan, and Forre's green eyes flicker to the King.
"A winged herald calling himself a servant of Prodyr," Alexander says, his voice cold. "He claims to be a divine messenger. The villages he burns are—" He doesn't finish. "He is the Empire's weapon."
Vallie's eye narrows. "One he can't control." She glances at the party. "And that's why they want you. Soldiers fight armies. You hunt monsters."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Prince Forre, what did your runner just tell you? And Your Majesty, how far east has the line slipped?

messages.name: Forre
messages.text:
Forre's head tilts, and he doesn't look up from the map. "A messenger's duty is to deliver news, not to explain it." His emerald eyes are fixed on the black token.
He traces the line of the token's new position with a fingertip, and doesn't smile. "The runner says the western front has moved. That's all."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."

Belle's jaw sets, and she shifts her weight. "The King's right to call us a scalpel," she says, her voice flat. "Forre's hammer will smash everything, but it won't find what we're looking for."
She looks at Max, then at the map. "We'll go behind the lines, find what's missing, and bring it back."
A beat, and her grin is all teeth. "And I'll have my axe in the skulls of that winged herald if he shows his face."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Prince Forre, you let that rumour about the Queen run through camp. Why haven't you put it down?

messages.name: Forre
messages.text:
Forre's green eyes flicker up from the map, and he doesn't smile. "A rumour is a fire. You don't put it out by pouring water on it. You starve it of oxygen."
He looks back at the map, his finger tracing the line of the token. "And I am not in the business of extinguishing fires that warm my house."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The court speaks. The court whispers. The court lies."
He doesn't say anything else.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Has anyone actually seen where the dead go after they leave their graves?

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The question hangs in the air, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room.
Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Guildmaster Vallie shifts her weight, her leather boots creaking on the stone floor.
The King stands still, his face a mask, his gaze fixed on the map table where the Zegallan banner hangs above.
A beat, and he speaks, his voice low and flat. "No one."
He looks at you, his eyes dark. "No one has seen where they go."
And the silence stretches, and the King does not look away.

The King's voice is sharp. "And we will end this rumour."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Then we take the King's commission. Point us at the front, Your Majesty.

messages.name: Alexander
messages.text:
Alexander's face does not soften, but there is a flicker of something in his eyes. "Very well."
He looks at Forre. "The commission is yours."
And he looks at you again. "And you will be remembered for your names."
The King turns, and his white fur mantle shifts as he walks away from the map table, his footsteps echoing in the war room.
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do not fail me."
He does not look back.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Belle, Dalan, get the horses. We ride for Fort Vicinitas tonight.

messages.name: Belle
messages.text:
"Finally." Belle's grin is sharp, and she cracks her knuckles. "Get the horses. We'll ride for Fort Vicinitas before dawn."
She glances at the map one more time, then at Forre. "We'll bring you back what you're looking for."
And she turns and leaves the war room, her boots heavy on the stone floor.
A beat, and the sound of her footsteps fades.
The room is quiet, and the smell of old banners and map parchment lingers.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride through the gate and report to whoever commands Fort Vicinitas.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The horses' hooves clatter on the stone as the party passes through the gate. The sentry steps aside, his spear-tip lowered.
The courtyard is empty, save for a few soldiers who are just stirring.
A man in plate armour stands at the far end of the courtyard, his face grim and his eyes hard. He is watching the party approach.
His armour is scarred and dented, and a longsword hangs at his hip.
He does not move as the party approaches, but his gaze is fixed on them.
And his voice is low and flat.
"You're the Crown's free company."
He doesn't wait for an answer.
"I am Captain Kaelen. I command this fort."
He looks at the party, his gaze lingering on Belle and Dalan.
"The Prince will be here by noon. Until then, you are under my command."
He looks at you.
"And we have much to discuss."

messages.text: The first gun speaks from across the valley just after dawn: a flat boom, a whistle, and a fountain of black earth fifty yards short of the ridge. Along the shield wall nobody flinches. They have heard it every morning for a month.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Captain, we heard the Zegallans sent someone under a parley flag. Take us to the parley.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:

"You're under my command," he says, and his voice is low. "And I'll tell you when you're ready."

He looks at you, and his eyes narrow. "And you're lucky I don't put you in the stocks for speaking to the Crown's army like that."
And he turns away.
The first gun speaks again: a flat boom, a whistle. And a fountain of black earth Fifty yards short of the ridge.

messages.name: Kanna
messages.text:
Kanna drives Blood Oath into the mud, her dark red eyes narrowing. "LOUD and fuckin' plain, then. You bury yours, I bury mine. My regiment keeps Greywater. Break it and I break you. I keep my word."
The Zegallan banner flutters in the wind, and there is no mistaking the sign.
A beat, and she shifts her weight. "And you've been diggin' up our dead at Greywater, too. Some new kind of sick-fuck game?"
The black steel of her armour gleams in the dawn light. "Or maybe the Darrans finally got the balls to send in someone worth killin'."
A beat, and her voice drops. "Which one is it?"

messages.text: Blood Saint, we're not the ones digging up your dead. Why do you care where the dead go?

messages.name: Kanna

She shifts her weight, and the black steel of her armour catches the light. "What I care about is the disrespect. And the cowardice."
A beat, and her fangs show. "A soldier earns their place in the dirt. And when someone goes digging, that's an insult to every man and woman who fell."
She looks at you, her dark red eyes cold and hard. "So you Darrans can't tell me why you're diggin', and you can't tell me what you're looking for. But you're gonna tell me if you're the ones who did it."
A beat, and her hand goes to Blood Oath. "And you're gonna do it fast."

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text: Zegallan banners from the last war hang above the palace map table. King Alexander names the villages lost on the Ashen March while Prince Forre marks a road to Fort Vicinitas in ink. Vallie has brought the Guild charter: the Crown wants a free company that can go where its army cannot. The council falls quiet, and every face at the table turns to you.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Princess Haley, do you believe the rumour about your mother?

messages.name: Haley
messages.text:
Haley's knuckles whiten against her fan. A beat, and her voice is ice. "The rumours are—" Her eyes flash. "The rumours are childish and base." Her posture stiffens as she turns her gaze from the King, from Forre, from Vallie. "My mother is not—" She stops, the words catching. The King's face is stone. Prince Forre's eyes are unreadable.
And Haley's jaw sets. She breathes, slow and quiet. She does not speak further.

messages.name: Alexander
messages.text:
Alexander's dark eyes narrow, and his hand falls away from the map table. "The Princess believes—" He doesn't finish the word. His face hardens, and a voice that has commanded armies rises. "This is a war council, not a gossip's den."
The King stands, and the silver of his crown gleams in the shadow of the Zegallan banners. "The missing dead will be looked into. But the matter is not here."
His gaze is not on Haley. It is on you. "The commission is this: Greywater, the Ashen March, the missing dead. The Guild's charter will see you through."
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do you accept?"

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Guildmaster Vallie, what is the Crown really asking of adventurers?

messages.name: Vallie
messages.text:
Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Crown's asking for a scalpel," she says, her voice blunt and low. "Where Forre's army goes in with a hammer, you're the ones who sneak in. The missing dead? That's what they want you to investigate. But make no mistake—they're sending you into the Empire's teeth."
She glances at the King, her expression unreadable. "The Crown will pay you, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park. It's a foray into enemy territory. You'll be behind their lines, and if you get caught..." She trails off, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room. "You'll be on your own."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: So who is burning the villages behind the line?

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
A murmur passes through the councillors. Haley's hand tightens on her fan, and Forre's green eyes flicker to the King.
"A winged herald calling himself a servant of Prodyr," Alexander says, his voice cold. "He claims to be a divine messenger. The villages he burns are—" He doesn't finish. "He is the Empire's weapon."
Vallie's eye narrows. "One he can't control." She glances at the party. "And that's why they want you. Soldiers fight armies. You hunt monsters."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Prince Forre, what did your runner just tell you? And Your Majesty, how far east has the line slipped?

messages.name: Forre
messages.text:
Forre's head tilts, and he doesn't look up from the map. "A messenger's duty is to deliver news, not to explain it." His emerald eyes are fixed on the black token.
He traces the line of the token's new position with a fingertip, and doesn't smile. "The runner says the western front has moved. That's all."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."

He looks up at Max, and his cheeks go pink. "But enough to hunt one or two monsters."

The room is silent, save for the soft crackle of the fire and the creak of a banner in the breeze.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride through the gate and report to whoever commands Fort Vicinitas.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The horses' hooves clatter on the stone as the party passes through the gate. The sentry steps aside, his spear-tip lowered.
The courtyard is empty, save for a few soldiers who are just stirring.
A man in plate armour stands at the far end of the courtyard, his face grim and his eyes hard. He is watching the party approach.
His armour is scarred and dented, and a longsword hangs at his hip.
He does not move as the party approaches, but his gaze is fixed on them.
And his voice is low and flat.
"You're the Crown's free company."
He doesn't wait for an answer.
"I am Captain Kaelen. I command this fort."
He looks at the party, his gaze lingering on Belle and Dalan.
"The Prince will be here by noon. Until then, you are under my command."
He looks at you.
"And we have much to discuss."

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text: Zegallan banners from the last war hang above the palace map table. King Alexander names the villages lost on the Ashen March while Prince Forre marks a road to Fort Vicinitas in ink. Vallie has brought the Guild charter: the Crown wants a free company that can go where its army cannot. The council falls quiet, and every face at the table turns to you.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Princess Haley, do you believe the rumour about your mother?

messages.name: Haley
messages.text:
Haley's knuckles whiten against her fan. A beat, and her voice is ice. "The rumours are—" Her eyes flash. "The rumours are childish and base." Her posture stiffens as she turns her gaze from the King, from Forre, from Vallie. "My mother is not—" She stops, the words catching. The King's face is stone. Prince Forre's eyes are unreadable.
And Haley's jaw sets. She breathes, slow and quiet. She does not speak further.

messages.name: Alexander
messages.text:
Alexander's dark eyes narrow, and his hand falls away from the map table. "The Princess believes—" He doesn't finish the word. His face hardens, and a voice that has commanded armies rises. "This is a war council, not a gossip's den."
The King stands, and the silver of his crown gleams in the shadow of the Zegallan banners. "The missing dead will be looked into. But the matter is not here."
His gaze is not on Haley. It is on you. "The commission is this: Greywater, the Ashen March, the missing dead. The Guild's charter will see you through."
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do you accept?"

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Guildmaster Vallie, what is the Crown really asking of adventurers?

messages.name: Vallie
messages.text:
Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Crown's asking for a scalpel," she says, her voice blunt and low. "Where Forre's army goes in with a hammer, you're the ones who sneak in. The missing dead? That's what they want you to investigate. But make no mistake—they're sending you into the Empire's teeth."
She glances at the King, her expression unreadable. "The Crown will pay you, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park. It's a foray into enemy territory. You'll be behind their lines, and if you get caught..." She trails off, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room. "You'll be on your own."

messages.text: So who is burning the villages behind the line?

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
A murmur passes through the councillors. Haley's hand tightens on her fan, and Forre's green eyes flicker to the King.
"A winged herald calling himself a servant of Prodyr," Alexander says, his voice cold. "He claims to be a divine messenger. The villages he burns are—" He doesn't finish. "He is the Empire's weapon."
Vallie's eye narrows. "One he can't control." She glances at the party. "And that's why they want you. Soldiers fight armies. You hunt monsters."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Prince Forre, what did your runner just tell you? And Your Majesty, how far east has the line slipped?

messages.name: Forre
messages.text:
Forre's head tilts, and he doesn't look up from the map. "A messenger's duty is to deliver news, not to explain it." His emerald eyes are fixed on the black token.
He traces the line of the token's new position with a fingertip, and doesn't smile. "The runner says the western front has moved. That's all."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."

He looks up at Max, and his cheeks go pink. "But enough to hunt one or two monsters."

The King's face is stone. Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Princess Haley's grip on her fan tightens until her knuckles are white.
The room is silent, save for the soft crackle of the fire and the creak of a banner in the breeze.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride through the gate and report to whoever commands Fort Vicinitas.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The horses' hooves clatter on the stone as the party passes through the gate. The sentry steps aside, his spear-tip lowered.
The courtyard is empty, save for a few soldiers who are just stirring.
A man in plate armour stands at the far end of the courtyard, his face grim and his eyes hard. He is watching the party approach.
His armour is scarred and dented, and a longsword hangs at his hip.
He does not move as the party approaches, but his gaze is fixed on them.
And his voice is low and flat.
"You're the Crown's free company."
He doesn't wait for an answer.
"I am Captain Kaelen. I command this fort."
He looks at the party, his gaze lingering on Belle and Dalan.
"The Prince will be here by noon. Until then, you are under my command."
He looks at you.
"And we have much to discuss."

messages.name: Kanna
messages.text:
Kanna's eyes narrow, and a beat, her teeth show. "My word is my word, Prince. And I keep my word."
A beat, and she shifts her weight, the black steel of her armour catching the light. "But I've seen too many Darran promises broken."
A beat, and her hand goes to Blood Oath, the greataxe that is her soul. "And if you break mine, then I'll kill you. I'll tear you apart."
And her voice is a snarl, and her fangs are sharp. "And I'll make you regret it."
A beat, and she looks at Forre, and her gaze is hard. "But I'll keep my word. Because I'm a soldier."
And her voice is flat, and there is no mistaking the promise. "And we're going to see who's lying."
A beat, and she doesn't look away from Forre.
